title: NSGo game scene (version 1)
description: SceneDoc is the root of a versioned YAML scene document.

version.description: Version is the schema version, from MinVersion to CurrentVersion. Encode writes it back as it is.

uid.description: UID is the scene file's stable ID, which stays the same when the file is renamed or moved so the tools can find it again (see package refs); empty until a tool such as game index gives it one. When set it must be a UID as resource.NewUID returns it. Resolve keeps the UID of the scene it resolves, not its base's. Both versions accept it.

name.description: Name is the scene's human-readable name.

virtualWidth.description: VirtualWidth and VirtualHeight are the scene's virtual viewport size in points. Both must be 0 or both positive.

virtualHeight.description: VirtualWidth and VirtualHeight are the scene's virtual viewport size in points. Both must be 0 or both positive.

backgroundColor.description: BackgroundColor is an optional CSS color string parsed with core.ParseColor.

camera.description: Camera holds the default camera transform for world-space layers. Nil leaves world space untransformed.

tilemaps.description: Tilemaps defines reusable named tilemaps referenced by layers via TilemapDoc.Ref.

layers.description: Layers are the scene's layers, drawn lowest Order first and in slice order for equal Order. In a scene that inherits another, a layer named like one of the base's adds its objects to that layer and may set nothing else (LayerOverrides changes the layer itself), and any other layer is added after the base's layers.

BoundsDoc.description: BoundsDoc is an axis-aligned rectangle in world coordinates.

x.description: X and Y are the rectangle's top-left corner.

y.description: X and Y are the rectangle's top-left corner.

width.description: Width and Height are the rectangle's size; both must be positive.

height.description: Width and Height are the rectangle's size; both must be positive.

CameraDoc.description: CameraDoc describes a 2D camera transform for world-space layers.

x.description: X and Y are the world coordinates centered in the virtual viewport (or mapped to the origin when virtual dimensions are 0).

y.description: X and Y are the world coordinates centered in the virtual viewport (or mapped to the origin when virtual dimensions are 0).

zoom.description: Zoom is the camera zoom factor; nil defaults to 1. Must be positive when set.

rotation.description: Rotation turns the camera clockwise in radians; world geometry rotates by -Rotation around (X, Y).

bounds.description: Bounds optionally clamps the camera view inside a world rectangle.

LayerDoc.description: LayerDoc is one ordered layer in a scene.

name.description: Name uniquely identifies the layer within the scene.

space.description: Space is SpaceWorld or SpaceScreen; empty defaults to SpaceWorld.

order.description: Order sets draw order across layers: lower values draw first, ties keep document order.

visible.description: Visible controls whether the layer draws; nil defaults to true.

tilemap.description: Tilemap optionally attaches a tilemap (by Ref, external Source, or inline grid) drawn beneath Objects.

objects.description: Objects are the placed objects in this layer.

ObjectDoc.description: ObjectDoc is one entity or visual object placed on a layer.

id.description: ID uniquely identifies the object across the entire scene.

name.description: Name is an optional human-readable display name.

prefab.description: Prefab optionally names a prefab or archetype template.

x.description: X and Y are where the object's origin sits in its parent's space, which for a top-level object is its layer's coordinate space.

y.description: X and Y are where the object's origin sits in its parent's space, which for a top-level object is its layer's coordinate space.

posZ.description: PosZ is the optional 3D Z coordinate (depth in 3D scenes) in its parent's space, distinct from 2D draw order Z.

originX.description: OriginX and OriginY are the pivot point inside the sprite's untrimmed frame.

originY.description: OriginX and OriginY are the pivot point inside the sprite's untrimmed frame.

rotation.description: Rotation turns the object clockwise in radians about its origin in 2D space.

rotX.description: RotX, RotY, and RotZ are optional 3D Euler rotations in radians about the X, Y, and Z axes, applied in that order about fixed axes (the rotation Rz * Ry * Rx).

rotY.description: RotX, RotY, and RotZ are optional 3D Euler rotations in radians about the X, Y, and Z axes, applied in that order about fixed axes (the rotation Rz * Ry * Rx).

rotZ.description: RotX, RotY, and RotZ are optional 3D Euler rotations in radians about the X, Y, and Z axes, applied in that order about fixed axes (the rotation Rz * Ry * Rx).

scaleX.description: ScaleX, ScaleY, and ScaleZ scale the object about its origin; nil defaults to 1. Negative mirrors.

scaleY.description: ScaleX, ScaleY, and ScaleZ scale the object about its origin; nil defaults to 1. Negative mirrors.

scaleZ.description: ScaleX, ScaleY, and ScaleZ scale the object about its origin; nil defaults to 1. Negative mirrors.

depth.description: Depth is the optional 3D extent along the Z axis in world units; 0 uses a default extent.

mesh.description: Mesh optionally names a 3D mesh primitive or asset path for 3D scene views.

flipX.description: FlipX and FlipY mirror the sprite inside its untrimmed frame box.

flipY.description: FlipX and FlipY mirror the sprite inside its untrimmed frame box.

alpha.description: Alpha is the object's opacity in [0, 1]; nil defaults to 1.

z.description: Z orders objects within the layer, children included; lower Z draws first, and ties keep document order with each parent before its children.

sprite.description: Sprite optionally binds the object to a frame in a sprite.Atlas.

material.description: Material optionally names a shared material resource file by its slash-separated path from the project root, such as "materials/stone.material.yaml". Build resolves it through a MaterialResolver; the sprite draws with the material's opacity and blend mode, so every scene that uses the file changes when it is edited.

components.description: Components holds structured component data keyed by component type name.

properties.description: Properties holds arbitrary custom metadata for gameplay scripts or editors.

children.description: Children are objects attached to this one, in document order. A child's transform (X, Y, Rotation, ScaleX, ScaleY, and in 3D PosZ, RotX, RotY, RotZ, ScaleZ) is local to this object, and its alpha multiplies this object's. Children belong to their parent's layer; their IDs share the scene-wide namespace, and nesting is limited to MaxObjectDepth levels.

SpriteRef.description: SpriteRef identifies one frame inside a named sprite.Atlas.

atlas.description: Atlas names the sprite.Atlas an AssetResolver looks up.

frame.description: Frame names the frame inside the atlas.

TilemapDoc.description: TilemapDoc describes either a reference to a named top-level tilemap (Ref), an external Tiled JSON map (Source), or an inline tile grid.

ref.description: Ref names an entry in SceneDoc.Tilemaps. Only valid on a layer's Tilemap.

source.description: Source is a path to an external Tiled .tmj file resolved by a TilemapResolver.

tileWidth.description: TileWidth and TileHeight are each tile's size in points for an inline grid.

tileHeight.description: TileWidth and TileHeight are each tile's size in points for an inline grid.

width.description: Width and Height are the inline grid dimensions in tiles.

height.description: Width and Height are the inline grid dimensions in tiles.

tileset.description: Tileset is the atlas name providing frames keyed by 1-based tile ID ("1", "2", ...).

data.description: Data holds Width*Height row-major tile IDs; 0 is an empty cell.
